tossups.text: One painting by this artist depicts a restaurant with a green ceiling and five customers hunched over tables. Among this artist's final works is his Wheatfield with Crows. Paintings such as The Yellow House were painted while this artist resided in Arles, during which he spent time with Paul Gauguin. This artist's still lifes include several depictions of sunflowers, and his later self-portraits show him with a bandaged ear. For 10 points, name the Dutch post-Impressionist who painted The Night Cafe and Starry Night.

One character in this novel is disturbed by an insulting figurine inscribed with the words "At Yo' Service" while working at the house of a family that wants to send her to Oberlin. Another character in this work describes his heart as a tin tobacco box and escapes from a chain gang in Alfred, Georgia. The protagonist of this novel marries Baby Suggs' son Halle, before giving birth to Denver while escaping from the Gardner owned Sweet Home Plantation. For 10 points, name this novel in which the title character returns to haunt Paul D and Sethe, her mother who mercy killed her to free her from slavery, a novel by Toni Morrison.

Several characters in this profession, including Crack, Dime, and the protagonist, discuss a film deal with Norman Oglesby and participate in a show with Destiny's Child at a Cowboys game in Ben Fountain's novel Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk. One character in this profession likes to suck on a white pebble from New Jersey sent to him by Martha and was a companion of Ted Lavender. Henry Dobbins, Curt Lemon, and Rat Kiley are people of this profession who appear in a short story collection whose namesake story is titled for objects like comic books, love letters, flak jackets, and jungle boots. For 10 points, name this profession of Jimmy Cross, the protagonist of Tim O'Brien's short story "The Things They Carried".

John Barth's Giles Goat-Boy contains a full-length parody of one play about him. In another work, he claims that Time destroys all but the gods before he disappears in his tomb while seeking refuge in Athens. In another, a shepherd tells him of Polybus's death and then reveals that Polybus adopted this club-footed man; he soon after blinds himself with some golden brooches after Jocasta commits suicide and he realizes that he killed Laius. For 10 points, name this Theban king and father of Antigone, the focus of two Sophocles plays.

This religion believes that the first human couple emerged from a rhubarb plant after the death of a man gave rise to different kinds of metal. According to this religion, the spiritual universe was created three thousand years before the egg-shaped physical universe, which had a single plant, a bull, and the first human. This religion states that, after death, the soul crosses over to the House of Song or House of Lies. A bearded man with wings, who may be a fravashi, is a symbol of this religion, whose funeral practices involve laying the body on a raised circular structure to be eaten by vultures. This religion, which worships in fire temples, has hymns called Gathas written in the liturgical language Avestan. For 10 points, name this dualistic Persian religion that worships Ahura Mazda.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for reflex arcs. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this spinal cord-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The spinal cord is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in reflex arcs.

tossups.text: Description acceptable. A god, potentially of bees, is depicted in this namesake manner in the Mayan ruins of Tulum. A teru teru bōzu may be placed in this manner to [emphasize] request rain. After Indra refuses to allow him to ascend in his physical body, Trishanku resides between heaven and earth in this manner. Thanatos and Hypnos are symbolized by torches depicted in this manner. Unable to play a flute in this manner, Marsyas ("MAR-see-us") loses a contest and is flayed by Apollo. Poseidon punishes Cassiopeia to sit on a throne in this manner half the time. Luck flows out if a horseshoe hangs in this manner. Considering himself unworthy of comparison to Jesus, Peter requests to be crucified in this manner. For 10 points, in popular culture, the symbol of a cross oriented in what manner is linked to Satanism?
acceptableAnswers: accept lying on one’s back after “Cassiopeia” is read
and prompt on descriptions of clinging to her throne by asking “why does she need to?”
accept a horseshoe with the open end pointing down after “horseshoe” is read

tossups.text: One type of cell in these structures has S-type and R-type anion channels which open to depolarize the membrane after an influx of potassium ions causes a conformational shift. These structures contain a spongy, permeable membrane below the upper palisade layer of cells. Stipules are attached near the petiole of these structures. The first step of C4 carbon fixation occurs in mesophyll cells in these structures. Reticulate veins in these structures are indicative of dicots. A cuticle on these structures prevents excess water loss through transpiration, which occurs in their stomata. For 10 points, name these plant structures where photosynthesis takes place.

In the Gospel of Luke, the rich man asks that Abraham would send a beggar with this name back to his family to warn them to live a better life, to which Abraham responds, "they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead." Coincidentally, the other person with this name in the New Testament is risen from the dead by Jesus. For 10 points, provide the shared name of these people from the New Testament.

Tourism to this historic compound usually includes visits to the towns of Zalesye and Kopachi and a tour of the Red Forest. This compound's New Safe Confinement was built in 2016 over a concrete sarcophagus around reactor number four. This compound's "elephant's foot" was discovered by "liquidators" in 1986. For 10 points, name this power plant near the town of Pripyat in Ukraine, the site of a massive nuclear disaster.

Adding cross-links to these substances can make them thermoset. These substances can be made through step-growth and chain-growth mechanisms. Wallace Carothers helped develop some of these substances for DuPont, which made many of them including Teflon, Kevlar, and nylon. These substances can occur naturally, as with cellulose and DNA, or be made synthetically, such as with plastics. For ten points, name these macromolecules that consist of repeating monomers.

This modern-day country was home to the bank robbers Carl Mezar, John Maxim, and a husband-and-wife duo called the "Foster Gang"; a manhunt to find them led to the Five Shilling Rebellion. A longtime politician in this country referred to his life philosophy as "holism," a notion that all organisms were interdependent; he ran on a pro-war ticket in this country to defeat Barry Hertzog and spoke at fundraisers for Israeli Zionist leader Chaim Weizmann. The Sauer Commission and the Fagan Commission published reports arguing for opposite policies in this modern county, where the Indian leader Mahatma Gandhi ran an Ambulance Corps at the Battle of Spion Kop. This country's longtime leader Jan Christian Smuts tried to discredit the "two streams" policy supported by his mentor Louis Botha. For 10 points, name this modern country that was split into provinces like the Cape Colony and Transvaal.

This dynasty saw a particularly chaotic time known as the period of "four moons and three kings," during which one king agreed to the Harmand treaty. One of its rulers sparked an incident by refusing to meet with the commander of the gunboat Cleopatra. That ruler symbolized the power of this family by ordering construction of the Nine Dynastic Urns, cast from bronze and associated with seven altars at a site called the "Temple of Generations." The first of its thirteen rulers came to power by defeating the Tay Son monarchy with help from the missionary Pierre Pigneau de Behaine. That ruler took the name Gia Long as a symbol of national unity in 1802, and this dynasty lasted until the abdication of Bao Dai in 1945. FTP, name this last ruling family in Vietnam.

Melanie Sanford's group has shown that this sort of reaction can be accomplished at room temperature under visible light using acyloxy-phthalimide initiators. The coupling discovered by Murai and Kakiuchi is a classic example of these reactions. Bis-pinacol-borane substituted on rhodium or ruthenium is a common catalyst for this type of reaction. Amines or imines are used as innate directors in directed ortho metalation, an example of this type of reaction. Shilov showed that a mix of potassium hexa-chloro-platinate mixed with potassium tetra-chloro-platinate can be used to accomplish this task, for example, to oxidize Zeise's salt. This process is accomplished by oxidative addition or sigma-bond metathesis, and an example of it would be turning ethane into ethanol. For 10 points, name this type of reaction in which a nonpolar bond found in all alkanes is cleaved and replaced by a reactive group.
acceptableAnswers: other synonyms of the word activation that mention both carbon and hydrogen

tossups.text: This leader declared that he was "prepared to die" for his ideals during the Rivonia Trial. For part of a 27 year prison sentence, this leader labored in a lime quarry while on Robben Island. This leader shared the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize with F. W. de Klerk for helping to end apartheid. For 10 points, what leader was the first black president of South Africa?

The winner of a national examination in 1930, he entered university where he was part of the "Anonymous Group." He settled for a time in the United States, although his negligence of a "no trespassing" sign, while discussing mathematics with his colleagues near a military radio transmitter on Long Island, resulted in an FBI record. For ten points, name this mathematician best known for his contributions to number theory and his elegant proofs of Bertrand's conjecture, Chebyshev's Theorem, and the Prime Number Theorem.

A substituent's impact on this general property for a molecule is plotted against its impact on hydrophobicity on a Craig plot. For hydrocarbons, this property is frequently measured in solutions of cesium cyclo·hexamide or in the gas phase using ion cyclotron resonance. Active methylene compounds have a high value for this property at the methylene. The sigma parameter in the first-ever linear free energy relationship describes how a substituent impacts this property of a molecule like nitroaniline. This property is unusually high for cyclopentadiene because its corresponding anion is aromatic. This property, which is described by the Hammett equation, increases when adjacent electronegative atoms are added in the inductive effect. This property has an exact inverse trend with p·K·a. For 10 point, name this propensity of a molecule to give up a proton.
acceptableAnswers: which is not a property of a molecule

tossups.text: These entities cannot be differentiated when they are inside of a MacAdam ellipse. Brent Berlin and Paul Kay wrote a book about basic terms for these entities. Ishihara plates are used to detect defects in seeing these entities, which, in HTML, are represented using a six-digit hexadecimal value. Printers use the CMYK model of these entities, which humans can see because of cone cells. For 10 points, name these entities that include red, green, and blue.

A narrator who visits the "White Friar" William Southfield then hears this author cite tears of contrition as proof of the Holy Ghost in that autobiographical narrator, who self-identifies with the phrase "this creature." This author's "Short Text" omits the parable of a servant who falls in a ditch and passages about "Christ our Mother." This author recounted receiving "all that is" in the form of a "little thing, the size of a hazelnut." The poem "Little Gidding" quotes this writer's statement that "All shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well." Margery Kempe wrote of visiting this author of the earliest surviving English book by a woman, which records sixteen "showings." For 10 points, Revelations of Divine Love is by what anchoress who lived in Norwich?

According to an essay by this man, novels chiefly serve as conduct manuals for "the young, the ignorant, and the idle." He argued that the line from Hamlet about "whips and scorns of time" should read "quips and scorns of title." In a poem, he called his home city the "needy villain's general home." "His only play, Irene, was a decisive failure. He wrote a poem which asks the reader to "remark each anxious Toil, each eager Strife, and watch the busy scenes of crowded Life." That poem, an imitation of Juvenal's tenth satire, is "The Vanity of Human Wishes." He wrote biographies of Richard Savage and many others, published as Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets. For 10 points, name this author much admired by Boswell, who wrote a famous dictionary.

parts.text: Name this Biblical figure who is depicted holding a sling in a Michelangelo sculpture showing him before he slays Goliath.
Michelangelo's David was displayed in public in this Italian city, a center of the Renaissance home to the Duomo cathedral and the Uffizi Gallery.
This other Italian artist's bronze David was the first freestanding male nude since antiquity. He is also known for depicting Erasmo Da Narni in his equestrian sculpture Gattamelata.

bonuses.leadin: This man carries a giant head on his back in a painting by Girolamo Forabosco. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel set in the village of Macondo. At the opening of this novel, a character remembers being taken to "discover ice" by his father José Arcadio.
acceptableAnswers: The One Hundred Years of Solitude

parts.text: In this novella by the author of One Hundred Years of Solitude, the Vicario brothers plot the assassination of Santiago Nasar to avenge an insult to their family.
acceptableAnswers: The Chronicle of a Death Foretold

parts.text: One Hundred Years of Solitude and Chronicle of a Death Foretold are by this Colombian magical realist author.

bonuses.leadin: A "biblical hurricane" destroys this novel's central location shortly after a boy born with a pig's tail is devoured by ants, fulfilling the prophecy of Melquíades's manuscript. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this short story in which Tom Kernan is led home by his friend Mr. Power after he falls down a flight of stairs while inebriated.
"Grace," along with "The Dead" and "The Gallants," appears in this author's short story collection Dubliners.

The narrator of this Joyce short story, also included in Dubliners, travels to the titular bazaar in an attempt to buy a gift for his friend Mangan's sister, with whom he is in love. The market turns out to be far from the romanticized vision of it that he imagined, however, and he finds that his love has faded away as well.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist is convinced by his friends to accompany them to a church service. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Italian author of works such as Foucault's Pendulum.
Eco is most famous for this work, a historical murder mystery that follows William of Baskerville, a 14th century monk.
Eco also wrote this 2010 historical novel that follows Simone Simonini, an author who is hired by Piedmont Government secret service to spy on Garibaldi.

bonuses.leadin: In one of this author's novels, Belbo, Diotallevi, and Casaubon create a conspiracy theory called "The Plan." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these animals, which Plato used two of to allegorize the human soul. After returning from court, Confucius once asked "was anyone hurt?" instead of asking about these animals.

The story about Confucius and news of a stable that burned down appears in this ancient Chinese philosophical text compiled by Confucius's followers that consists of stories about Confucius and his students.
Gongsun Long describes his coming of age in book 17 of this text. The last chapter of this text lists the "Ten Paradoxes" of School of Names philosopher Hui Shi.

bonuses.leadin: A dialogue authored by Gongsun Long debates whether a white one of these animals is one of these animals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with defecation reflex.
What is the main function of the colon in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to defecation reflex.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Using forms such as a court trial and a jump rope rhyme, twelve hanged maids interrupt Penelope's experience during The Odyssey in The Penelopiad by this Canadian author of Cat's Eye and The Handmaid's Tale.

In this author's Ragnarok: The End of the Gods, a child evacuated from the Blitz reads a book of Norse myth. She also wrote about the relationship of Randolph Ash and Christabel LaMotte in Possession.

This author's Dream Angus contains several modern and one archaic story about a Celtic god who is turned into a swan. He created the Botswanan investigator Precious Ramotswe for The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series.

bonuses.leadin: Name some things about the Canongate Myth series, in which contemporary authors were recruited to rewrite old myths, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this organ, connected to the cervix at its lower portion and the fallopian tubes at its upper portion.

This temporary organ forms in the uterus during pregnancy and regulates nutrient exchange. The immunity barrier this organ provides prevents the mother's immune system from attacking the fetus as a foriegn object.
The placenta forms after a blastocyst binds to this inner lining of the uterus, otherwise shed during menstruation.

bonuses.leadin: If cancer is found in this organ, a hysterectomy may be performed. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this term for the philosophical tendency to doubt something, particularly beliefs regarding knowledge.
Skepticism is important within this branch of philosophy, which seeks to understand and define knowledge.

Skeptics often argue against the use of this concept, often described as a universally agreeable judgment orknowledge, as an argument. Beyond philosophy, this concept is most familiar as the title of a 1776 pamphlet byAmerican colonist Thomas Paine.

bonuses.leadin: People who advocated this type of thought included ancient Greeks like Sextus Empiricus and modernempiricists like David Hume. For ten points each,

parts.text: Identify this SEC university, nicknamed the Crimson Tide, who has won three of the last six national championships. It is located in Tuscaloosa and contests the Iron Bowl with in-state rivals Auburn.

Alabama is led by this legendary coach, often considered one of the greatest college coaches of all time. In the 2017 special election for Senate in Alabama, this man received thousands of write-in votes, which may have helped swing the election for Doug Jones.
In 2013, Alabama lost the Iron Bowl on the last play of the game after Chris Davis scored a 109-yard touchdown in this manner to win the game for Auburn. A description is acceptable.
acceptableAnswers: anything about a field goal return

bonuses.leadin: This team beat Ohio State to win the 2020 college football national championship. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This effect is the decrease in energy and increase in wavelength of an x-ray or gamma ray photon when it interacts with matter. Its discovery demonstrates that light cannot be explained purely as a wave.
This effect is seen in the levitation of a metal sample above a superconductor cooled by liquid nitrogen; the samples are shown to display diamagnetism as all internal magnetic field were cancelled.

This effect is the production of a voltage difference across an electrical conductor that is transverse to an electric field. When that voltage is quantized, the quantum variety of this effect is observed.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify some eponymous effects in physics.

parts.text: Name this colony which was founded in 1607 by a group including John Smith.
Jamestown was nearly abandoned after the period known as this during the winter of 1609-1610. During it, Powhatan's attempts to deprive the settlers of food resulted in a nearly 80% death rate.
Pocahontas and Powhatan, the leaders of the Powhatan Confederacy, were members of this tribe. Their queen Cockacoeske signed the Articles of Peace in 1677 after Bacon's Rebellion.

bonuses.leadin: The ships that settled this colony were the Susan Constant, the Godspeed and the Discovery, which were commanded by Christopher Newport. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ethnicity shared by Oscar Banker and by a person who came up with the phrase "government is not the solution to our problem; government is the problem" as the head writer of the first inaugural address by Ronald Reagan.
The aforementioned speechwriter, Ken Khachigian, acted as a senior advisor to this other Armenian‑American, who was the governor of California from 1983 to 1991.

After George Deukmejian removed himself from consideration as George H.W. Bush's running mate in 1988, Bush ultimately chose this senator from Indiana. Lloyd Bentsen told this man "Senator, you're no Jack Kennedy."

bonuses.leadin: A person of this ethnicity became known as "the man who made Ralph Nader" because he invented the P-R-N-D-L shift pattern for automatic transmissions. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of computer technology for storing, processing, and presenting spatial data.

ArcGIS was developed by this largest vendor of geographic information systems software, founded by Jack and Laura Dangermond. It hosts an annual International User's Conference and developed the vector Shapefile format.

Along with LIDAR and aerial imaging, these kinds of maps were among the tools used to produce Digital Elevation Models, which facilitated the development of GIS. They represent elevation using contour lines.

bonuses.leadin: The father of this technology was Roger Tomlinson, who used it to map land use and soils during the Canada Land Inventory. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man who described a world without lawyers in Utopia.
More was a councilor to this man before being executed by him. This monarch ordered the dissolution of the monasteries and created the Anglican Church after divorcing the first of his six wives.
Henry VIII's second wife was this woman, whom he beheaded. Her daughter with Henry, Elizabeth I, later served as queen as well.

bonuses.leadin: This man denied the validity of the Act of Supremacy and refused to take the Oath of Supremacy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The first noble gas compound was synthesized by reacting this element with platinum hexafluoride. This element has atomic number number 54 and symbol Xe, and can form compounds with oxygen and fluorine.
The first discovered binary compound of a noble gas, xenon tetrafluoride, has this molecular geometry that has four ninety degree bond angles.
Xenon difluoride can react with various metallic compounds to form these molecules that usually consist of a central metal ion bonded to surrounding ligands.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about compounds of noble gases, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name these proteins which bind to receptors that have been activated by immune proteins such as interferons, thus mediating a signaling pathway by which extracellular cytokines regulate transcription.
acceptableAnswers: Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription

parts.text: The STAT protein family is activated by JAK, which is one of these proteins. The ErbB family contains examples of the "receptor" type of these proteins, which preferentially target phenol groups.
Drugs which inhibit the JAK-STAT pathway, including Ruxolitinib, can be used to treat myelofibrosis, a cancer of this tissue which possesses hematopoietic stem cells.

bonuses.leadin: Proteins in the CIS family are cytokine-induced inhibitors of these proteins, which dimerize via interactions between their phosphorylated SH2 domains. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this orbital that can hold less electrons than the p, d, or f orbitals.
Unlike p orbitals, which are shaped like dumbbells, s orbitals are shaped like these objects.
Post-transition metals such as thallium have an oxidation state two less than their valency due to this effect, which is caused by the electrons in the outermost s orbital being difficult to ionize.

bonuses.leadin: The azimuthal quantum number for this orbital equals zero. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this British playwright who used silence to undercut Max's monologue in The Homecoming, but also developed a distinctive brand of dialogue in plays such as The Dumbwaiter and The Caretaker.

Theater critic Irving Wardle adapted the subtitle of David Compton's play The Lunatic View to characterize Pinter's Birthday Party as this kind of comedy, whose characters joke about impending threats.
In The Homecoming, Pinter included a notable pause immediately afer Ruth refuses to give Lenny this object and warns him "if you take [this object] . . . I'll take you."
acceptableAnswers: any other synonym suggesting a vessel of water

bonuses.leadin: In this author's speech before the 1962 National Student Drama Festival, he outlined two diferent kinds of silence in his plays. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this series featuring 19th century Russian intellectual figures such as Alexander Herzen and Ivan Turgenev which is made up of the plays Voyage, Shipwreck, and Salvage.
The Coast of Utopia trilogy was written by this Czech-born British playwright of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead.
Vladimir Lenin appears in this Stoppard play in which Henry Carr reminiscences about his encounters with figures like James Joyce and Tristan Tzara while living in Zurich in 1917.

bonuses.leadin: This series of plays, for which its author won the fourth of his five Tony Awards for Best Play, takes its title from a book by Avrahm Yarmolinsky. For 10 points each:
